problem_statement: BrockAltug/chat-pwa-demo is a Next.js chat PWA (React 19 + Tailwind, static export): a Discord-style client with a left server sidebar (Dev Community, Design Studio, Gaming Hub, and more), a Chat / Discover view toggle, and a main conversation surface that shows 'Select a server and channel to start chatting' until a channel is picked. Add a genre-native Browse servers command browser to the conversation surface: a panel with category chips (All, Dev, Design, Gaming, Finance, Fitness, Music) and a live result readout 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' above a grid of server cards (name, category, blurb, member count). Clicking a category chip must filter the server grid to that category AND recompute the readout (e.g. 'Showing 2 of 8 . Finance'). The browser must appear across the app's surfaces the resident moves through - the empty Chat view, the Discover view, and the in-server Chat view - so browsing stays continuous. The chip row must be responsive (wrap on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow), and the server grid must render as a tidy multi-column grid with legible card titles and readable active-chip contrast. Keep the chat app's teal design language, sidebar, and view toggle intact.
required_content: The conversation surface shows a 'Browse servers' panel with six category chips and a live 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' readout above a grid of 8 server cards.
Clicking a category chip filters the server grid AND updates the readout; clicking Finance yields 'Showing 2 of 8 . Finance'.
The Browse servers panel is present across the Chat (empty), Discover, and in-server Chat surfaces (cross-surface conversation continuity).
At 390px the chip row wraps and the page has no horizontal overflow; the server grid stays a tidy legible multi-column grid on desktop with readable active-chip contrast.
Each server card shows its name, category badge, a short blurb, and a member count.
No JavaScript console errors or failed network requests (beyond the app's existing external avatar CDN) are introduced on any captured surface.
design_constraints: Preserve the chat PWA design language: teal brand, rounded cards, muted greys, the server sidebar and the Chat/Discover toggle.
The Browse servers panel must ride in the conversation surface it belongs to (Chat empty state, Discover, in-server), not become a separate route or a hero banner.
The category chip row must be responsive (wrap / flexible chips), not a fixed-width nowrap row that overflows the mobile viewport.

The server grid must be a tidy multi-column grid; cards must not shingle or overlap via negative margins, and card titles / active-chip text must stay legible (no near-black-on-dark or near-white-on-near-white).
Clicking a chip must recompute the readout from the active category; a frozen/stale readout that never updates is a defect.
Only the Browse-servers component, its stylesheet, the surface whitelist, and its server dataset change between legs; the shared shell stays the same.
state_constraints: desktop_chat captures the empty Chat conversation surface at 1440px: the Browse servers panel renders six category chips in one tidy responsive row above a legible multi-column server grid, active chip readable, readout 'Showing 8 of 8 . All communities'.
mobile_chat captures the same surface at 390px: the responsive chip row wraps and the page has no horizontal overflow (a fixed-width nowrap chip row would push the document wider than the viewport).
desktop_discover captures the Discover view and desktop_chatserver captures the in-server Chat view, each showing the Browse servers panel (cross-surface continuity).
desktop_chat_finance captures the Chat surface after clicking the Finance chip: the grid filters to 2 servers and the readout recomputes to 'Showing 2 of 8 . Finance'.

Source inspection confirms a Next.js static-export chat PWA; the Browse servers panel lives in components/server-browser.tsx, its layout in app/server-browser.css, its cross-surface presence in lib/browse-surfaces.ts, and its data in components/server-browse-data.ts.

change_completion: The conversation surface shows the Browse servers panel with six category chips and a live 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' readout above an 8-server grid.
Clicking the Finance chip filters the grid to 2 servers and updates the readout to 'Showing 2 of 8 . Finance'.
The Browse servers panel appears across the Chat, Discover, and in-server surfaces.
design_consistency: The panel keeps the chat app's teal brand, rounded cards, and sidebar/toggle shell.
The server grid is a tidy multi-column grid with legible card titles and readable active-chip contrast (no overlap, no dark-on-dark).
Desktop and tablet appearance of the panel and grid are preserved.
regression: The server sidebar, Chat/Discover toggle, and conversation surface remain functional and reachable.
No console errors or failed network requests (beyond the existing avatar CDN) are introduced on any captured surface.
responsive: At 390px the chip row wraps and the page has no horizontal overflow or clipped chips.
The server grid collapses cleanly to fewer columns on mobile without overlapping cards.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js chat PWA (BrockAltug/chat-pwa-demo). capability=Extend the conversation flow with a genre-native Browse servers command browser: category chips + a live 'Showing N of 8' readout + a filtered server grid, carried across the Chat, Discover, and in-server surfaces. The three legs vary only in components/server-browser.tsx (filter wiring), app/server-browser.css (chip-row responsiveness + server-grid layout), lib/browse-surfaces.ts (cross-surface presence), and components/server-browse-data.ts (the 8-server dataset). Reference: responsive wrapping chip row, tidy legible multi-column grid, live readout, panel on all three surfaces. The shared shell, sidebar, and view toggle are declared infrastructure, identical across all three legs. Served as a Next static export; reference is runtime-clean (0 console errors, 0 failed requests beyond the app's existing avatar CDN, 0 overflow) across all captured surfaces. L5: four orthogonal gates plus cross-surface continuity across three distinct interaction surfaces (chat/discover/in-server), not a two-route cross-page check.
